chapter.name: Sets
chapter.blurb: This chapter introduces a set as a well-defined collection of objects and the roster and set-builder ways of writing one. It then studies the empty set, finite, infinite and equal sets, subsets (including intervals as subsets of R) and the universal set, and closes with the operations of union, intersection, difference and complement, illustrated with Venn diagrams and summed up in De Morgan's laws.

scope_in.item: Decide whether a described collection is well-defined (a set), and use x in A / x not in A for membership, including the standard sets N, Z, Q, R, Z+, Q+, R+

Write a set in roster form (distinct elements, order immaterial, dots for an infinite pattern) and in set-builder form {x : property}, convert between the two, and find solution sets of simple equations
Recognise the empty (null, void) set phi = { }, and show a set-builder description is empty by giving the reason no element qualifies
Classify sets as finite or infinite (an empty set is finite), use n(S) for the number of distinct elements of a finite set, and know that some infinite sets such as R cannot be written in roster form
Decide whether two sets are equal (exactly the same elements; repetition and order do not matter) and pick out equal pairs from a list

Test whether A subset of B, use proper subset, superset and singleton set, the facts that phi subset of every set and A subset of A, A subset of B and B subset of A iff A = B, and distinguish 'is an element of' from 'is a subset of' for sets whose elements are themselves sets
List all subsets of a set with at most three elements by direct enumeration
Use the subsets N, Z, Q, T (irrationals) of R and the relations N subset of Z subset of Q, Q subset of R, T subset of R, N not a subset of T

Use open, closed and one-end-closed intervals (a, b), [a, b], [a, b), (a, b] and rays such as [0, infinity), (-infinity, 0), convert between interval and set-builder form, compare intervals as subsets, and find the length b - a
Propose a suitable universal set for given sets and represent U by a rectangle and its subsets by circles in a Venn diagram (regions described in words)

Find the union and intersection of sets (roster or set-builder), identify disjoint sets, and use the union and intersection laws: commutative, associative, identity, idempotent, laws of phi and U, and the distributive law A intersection (B union C) = (A intersection B) union (A intersection C)
Find the difference A - B and B - A, use A - B = {x : x in A and x not in B}, and use that A - B, A intersection B, B - A are mutually disjoint
Find the complement A' with respect to U (finite U, or U = N), use A' = U - A, the complement laws, double complementation, phi' = U and U' = phi, and verify De Morgan's laws

Prove or disprove simple set statements by element arguments or counterexamples (e.g. A union B = A intersection B implies A = B; A intersection B = A intersection C need not imply B = C; the equivalence of A subset of B, A - B = phi, A union B = B, A intersection B = A)

concepts.name: Sets and their representations
concepts.description: A set as a well-defined collection of objects, the notation x in A / x not in A, and the two ways of writing a set: roster (tabular) form and set-builder form.
concepts.idea: A set is a well-defined collection of objects: for any object we can definitely decide whether it belongs to the collection or not.
concepts.rule: Roster form lists the distinct elements, separated by commas, inside braces { }; order does not matter and elements are not repeated. Set-builder form {x : property} uses a property possessed by every element of the set and by no element outside it; the braces mean 'the set of all' and the colon means 'such that'.
concepts.example: {x : x is a natural number and 3 < x < 10} = {4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}; the set of letters of SCHOOL is {S, C, H, O, L}.

concepts.name: Empty, finite, infinite and equal sets
concepts.description: The empty (null, void) set, finite and infinite sets with n(S) as the number of distinct elements, and equal sets as sets having exactly the same elements.
concepts.idea: The empty set phi = { } has no elements. A set is finite if it is empty or has a definite number of elements; otherwise it is infinite.
concepts.rule: A = B exactly when A and B have the same elements; repeating elements or changing their order does not change a set. The empty set counts as a finite set.
concepts.example: {x : x is a natural number and 1 < x < 2} = phi (finite); the set of letters of ALLOY equals the set of letters of LOYAL, both {A, L, O, Y}.

concepts.name: Subsets, proper subsets and subsets of R
concepts.description: A subset of B as a set all of whose elements lie in B, proper subsets and supersets, singleton sets, the difference between 'is an element of' and 'is a subset of', listing all subsets of a small set, and the subsets N, Z, Q, T of R.
concepts.idea: A is a subset of B when every element of A is also an element of B. Every set is a subset of itself and phi is a subset of every set.
concepts.rule: A subset of B and B subset of A if and only if A = B. If A subset of B and A is not equal to B, A is a proper subset of B and B is a superset of A. An element of a set (x in A) is not the same as a subset ({x} subset of A).
concepts.example: {1, 3} subset of {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}; {a} subset of {a, b, c} but {a} is not an element of {a, b, c}; N subset of Z subset of Q subset of R.

concepts.name: Intervals as subsets of R
concepts.description: Open, closed and one-end-closed intervals (a, b), [a, b], [a, b), (a, b] as subsets of R, converting between interval and set-builder notation, rays such as [0, infinity), and the length b - a of an interval.
concepts.idea: For real numbers a < b, an interval is the set of all real numbers between a and b; a round bracket excludes the end point and a square bracket includes it.
concepts.rule: (a, b) = {x : a < x < b}, [a, b] = {x : a <= x <= b}, [a, b) = {x : a <= x < b}, (a, b] = {x : a < x <= b}. Each has length b - a and contains infinitely many points.
concepts.example: {x : x in R, -5 < x <= 7} = (-5, 7], of length 12; [0, infinity) is the set of non-negative real numbers.
